mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 8% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 6-month moving average, combined with a concurrent rise in personal savings (RSAFS), signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction and retail spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 6-mo moving average AND RSAFS > 6-mo moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its trend for four consecutive months indicates robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) combined with a simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two quarters signals a deepening economic recession, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
